The core challenge is reconciling conflicting statistical claims within the coaching lane. The short-week deficit signal exhibits self-inconsistency between its docstring range and coded value, indicating potential overfitting or miscommunication. The market-inference split confounds separate information flows, while the calibration gate assumes static performance thresholds that may not hold under distributional shifts. These primitives form a network of failure modes: overconfident point estimates leak into published confidence, and static gates fail to adapt to changing data patterns. Resolving these requires grounding projections in backtested empirical distributions rather than relying on ad-hoc adjustments.
